title: A Window Box in Bloom
description: Explore a small planted box through its container fittings, trailing growth, and familiar annual flowers.
cardDescription: Explore a small planted box through its container fittings, trailing growth, and familiar annual flowers.
focus: A window box combines a container with plants chosen for a small visible space. The clues distinguish a trailing habit, a supporting fitting, and the flowers themselves.
solvingTip: Use the plant or object category before the color or position clue.
words: Narrow planter placed beneath a window, with spaces omitted
Familiar annual flower with trumpet-shaped blooms
Small-flowered plant often used for blue edging or trailing growth
Support fixed beneath a projecting planted box
Describing stems that hang or spread over a planter's edge
Color between blue and purple seen in some container blooms
Growing material filling the planted container
To allow excess water to pass from a container
Plant organ anchoring growth inside a box
Open flower displayed above the planter's rim
Upper edge of a planted container
Green plant part along a flowering stem
Plant reproductive structure from which an annual can grow
Bright daisy-family flower grown in many summer containers

answerNotes.WINDOWBOX: Window box is written without its space in the grid; it describes the container's position rather than a plant species.
answerNotes.PETUNIA: Petunias are common container plants; their colors and growth habits vary among varieties.
answerNotes.LOBELIA: Garden lobelias include several forms; the familiar bedding types are the focus here.
answerNotes.BRACKET: A bracket supports the container, while the plant's roots occupy the growing medium inside it.
answerNotes.TRAILING: Trailing describes a growth habit, not a single plant family.

title: A Garden in Dappled Shade
description: Recognize plants and features of a garden receiving filtered light beneath trees.
cardDescription: Recognize plants and features of a garden receiving filtered light beneath trees.
focus: Shade gardens vary in moisture and light levels. The clues use distinctive plant forms and plain definitions rather than assuming every shaded place has identical growing conditions.
solvingTip: Look for the leaf or flower shape named in the clue, then use short setting words.
words: Garden plant grown especially for its broad leaves
Shade-garden plant with feathery flower plumes
Nonflowering plant with leaves often called fronds
Overhead layer of leaves filtering sunlight below
Marked by patches of light and shade
Small nonflowering plant forming low green mats
Flat foliage part especially valued on many hostas
Covering layer spread on the soil around plants
Prepared area where the garden plants grow
Tall woody plant casting shade over a border
Long seat placed beside the shaded path
Below-ground structure shared by garden plants and trees
Open flower appearing among broad foliage

answerNotes.HOSTA: Hostas are often grown for foliage, although they also produce flowers.
answerNotes.ASTILBE: Astilbe is recognized by its plume-like flower clusters; different varieties flower at different times.
answerNotes.FERN: A fern reproduces by spores rather than flower seeds.
answerNotes.CANOPY: Canopy describes the leaf layer, not the garden's ground surface.
answerNotes.DAPPLED: Dappled light forms a patchwork rather than uninterrupted full sun or complete darkness.

title: Small Plants in a Rock Garden
description: Explore low-growing plants among stones through crevices, gravel, and spreading cushions of foliage.
cardDescription: Explore low-growing plants among stones through crevices, gravel, and spreading cushions of foliage.
subtheme: Small Plants in a Rock Garden
focus: A rock garden uses the spaces around stones as part of its design. Some plants form mats or store water, while the supporting materials have their own descriptive names.
solvingTip: Distinguish a plant name from the size or arrangement of the stones around it.
words: Succulent plant group often grown among stones
Narrow gap between stones where a small plant may grow
Loose small stones used around rock-garden plants
Rounded compact growth form of some rock-garden plants
Describing a plant associated with high mountain habitat
Hard natural piece forming a rock garden's structure
Coarse mineral particles added to some growing mixtures
Low green plant growing in some sheltered stone gaps
Aromatic herb whose creeping kinds can form low mats
Circular cluster of leaves spreading from a short center
Plant part extending into a crack's growing material
Inclined surface among the garden's stones
To allow water to move through a growing mixture
Open flower above a small rock-garden plant

answerNotes.SEDUM: Sedums store water in fleshy tissue; their varied forms include familiar low-growing garden kinds.
answerNotes.CREVICE: A crevice is a space, not a particular soil ingredient.
answerNotes.GRAVEL: Gravel consists of mineral pieces; it differs from compost or other organic additions.
answerNotes.CUSHION: Cushion describes the plant's shape and habit rather than naming one species.
answerNotes.ALPINE: Alpine is a habitat word; not every plant used in a rock garden is truly alpine.

title: Fragrance Beside the Garden Gate
description: Meet aromatic garden plants through their leaves, flowers, and familiar culinary connections.
cardDescription: Meet aromatic garden plants through their leaves, flowers, and familiar culinary connections.
focus: Fragrance can come from foliage as well as flowers. The clues identify particular plants through recognizable descriptions, with no claim that a scent has a medical effect.
solvingTip: Use whether the clue mentions leaves, flower clusters, or a familiar kitchen herb.
words: Aromatic plant known for narrow leaves and purple flower spikes
Shrub with fragrant spring flower clusters, often pale purple
Plant group containing many strongly fragrant flowering vines and shrubs
Fragrant shrub herb with narrow leaves, often paired with roast potatoes
Aromatic herb group including peppermint and spearmint
Aromatic herb with often gray-green leaves used in stuffing
Fragrance noticed when passing a flowering garden
Plant part crushed or brushed to release many herb aromas
Support carrying aromatic leaves and flowers
Open flower adding color beside the gate
Walking route passing the scented border
Hinged entrance beside this fragrant planting
Flowering shrub with many fragrant varieties

answerNotes.LAVENDER: Lavender's fragrance can come from its foliage and flowers; the name covers multiple species and varieties.
answerNotes.LILAC: Lilac also names a color, but its flowers can appear in several shades.
answerNotes.JASMINE: Many jasmines are fragrant, but the group does not share one identical flower color or growth habit.
answerNotes.ROSEMARY: Rosemary is an herb shrub; its leaf shape differs from the broad leaves of mint.
answerNotes.MINT: Mint names a plant group, while the flavor can also appear in foods and manufactured products.

title: A Meadow for Pollinators
description: Explore a flowering meadow through familiar plants, nectar visitors, and the habitat around them.
cardDescription: Explore a flowering meadow through familiar plants, nectar visitors, and the habitat around them.
focus: A meadow contains more than one kind of flowering plant. The clues distinguish nectar from pollen and identify a few recognizable plants without prescribing one universal seed mixture.
solvingTip: Match the flower name or insect role first. A food material is different from the visitor collecting it.
words: Plant group whose members are hosts for monarch caterpillars
Daisy-like flower with a prominent raised central disk
Plant with clusters of small yellow flowers in late summer or fall
Sweet floral liquid gathered by many pollinating insects
Powder carrying a flowering plant's male reproductive cells
Late-season daisy-family flower with a star-suggesting name
Flower-visiting insect that can transfer pollen
Flying insect whose adult may visit meadow flowers at night
Narrow-leaved plant growing between meadow flowers
Reproductive structure produced after many meadow flowers mature
Plant support holding leaves and flower heads
Open meadow flower available to visiting insects
Place supplying the conditions and resources an organism uses
Plant structure extending below the meadow surface

answerNotes.MILKWEED: Monarch caterpillars feed on milkweeds; suitable species and growing conditions vary by region.
answerNotes.CONEFLOWER: Coneflower describes several familiar garden plants; purple coneflower is one well-known example.
answerNotes.GOLDENROD: Goldenrods include many species; their yellow clusters are distinct from a single large sunflower head.
answerNotes.NECTAR: Nectar supplies sugars, while pollen serves a different reproductive role in the plant.
answerNotes.POLLEN: Pollen and nectar are separate materials, even when the same insect collects both.
